summary.text: Son of Laomedon (`laomedon`) and brother of Priam and Hicetaon (`hicetaon-trojan`), who sat with the elders at the Scaean gates — distinct from Clytius the suitors (`clytius-same`, `clytius-zacynthus`) and from the father of Dolops among the Danaan leaders (`dolops-clytiid`).

story.text: When Helen came to the wall, Clytius sat among the elders about Priam — Panthous, Thymoetes, Lampus, Hicetaon, scion of Ares, Ucalegon, and Antenor — men of prudence who had ceased from battle for old age but spoke full sweet at the Scaean gates.

Aeneas, vaunting his lineage to Achilles, counts Clytius among the sons whom peerless Laomedon begat beside Tithonus, Priam, and Hicetaon, scion of Ares — the blood from which he avows himself sprung through Assaracus and Anchises.
